features.label: Features overview
features.tagline: Key capabilities · aligned with the current in-app manual
features.intro: WinProx is one Facility web app: issues come in, become tasks, and are handled by teams. Time (punch clock) is included.
features.source: Sources: Manual (Getting started + chapters) and FAQ in the app.
features.footer_right: See also: Technical fact sheet (hosting, GDPR, security)

left.title: Issues
left.body: Via unit QR, manually in admin, or (with IoT) a sensor alarm. Filters, approval of QR reports, recurring maintenance (pause or close). Optional: required contact details and/or email confirmation for anonymous QR reporters (category and unit; confirmation holds the report until the email link). On public QR pages visible only after approval; admin sees everything immediately. In admin a Reporter confirmed pill appears when the QR reporter confirmed the email link. Optional per category: hide previous/open reports on the unit QR.

left.title: Tasks
left.body: One issue → one or more tasks, each for one team. Priority, due date, notes. Follow-up via the Tasks list and QR on the floor.

left.title: Resolution
left.body: Updates on issues and tasks, complete a task (optional photo and note), close the issue when everything is done. Status and history in the back office; workers resolve via unit QR, or via Clock Point with an open GPS work visit at that location.

left.title: Facility
left.body: Locations, units, categories, teams and workers (internal or external). Under Places: Categories, Locations and Units (tenant-wide). Bulk/CSV import (bulk also sets advanced portal options for the whole range), dashboard, documents and announcements on the portal. Enable unit checks per category and unit; manage checklists under People → Teams — shared or per team. New organisations can load a starter template on the dashboard (at your own locations, at customer sites, or for vehicles and fleet) with sample teams, categories, a location, units and matching work menu defaults — names in every language. You can rename everything later; once issues exist, units can only be deactivated. Under People → Workers: search screen for all workers. Workers and employees can be linked to sites; floater teams may clock in anywhere. Optional portrait photo per worker (automatically resized); shown in Teams, Workers and Time → Presence. Rare actions (team leader, icon/phone/PIN, deactivate, delete) live in the edit modal, not on the team list.

left.title: Dashboard
left.body: Overview of open issues and today's tasks, with quick access to key workflows. New organisations pick a starter template here; briefing and reports are available from the dashboard.

left.title: QR portals
left.body: Unit QR: report issues, plus an optional unit check (quick OK or Not OK). Clock Point QR: sign in (name + icon) and team tasks; clock in/out only with Time (punch clock). Location QR. Printable as sticker sheet (Avery) or full-page A6/A5/A4. Dynamic QRs that can be linked to a unit later. Invalid or expired QR codes show a short error with a button to the homepage. Per category you can hide previous reports on the unit QR. Workers who opened the unit QR online can start and complete tasks, create a report (with photos) and do a unit check without coverage; those actions stay on the device and sync automatically when the connection returns. Clock in/out at Clock Point stays online and still needs a fresh QR scan. With GPS work visits you can start and complete team tasks on Clock Point and do the next inspection stop (unit check) on site. Name + icon is who you are; clock-in (Time) is your shift. Unit check on Clock Point only after Start work at that location.

left.title: Unit checks
left.body: Quickly confirm a unit is fine — for example after a security round, cleaning check or technical inspection. On the unit QR you tap OK or Not OK; OK needs no separate issue. Optionally tick a checklist first. Not OK still works alongside the normal report flow.

left.title: Inspection rounds
left.body: Recurring issue with a fixed route of units (stops), including across locations. Plan via Work → Inspection rounds → Plan inspection round (stops, interval and team in one step), or via Issues or the issue wizard. Work → Inspection rounds is its own list of rounds only, not ordinary issues. Only units with unit checks appear in the stop list; other units are hidden. Set the route order with the numbered stop list (tick and drag in the same list; 1 = first stop). One task per cycle; at each stop Unit check OK, Not OK (with issue; description prefilled), or skip with reason. Done when all stops for that cycle are handled. With Time + GPS work visits, today's round location appears after clock-in on Clock Point → Where do I need to go today. Open tasks shows description, priority, status and the next stop. The Unit check button appears only after Start work at that location; the full check opens after that button, without the unit QR.

left.title: Unit measurements
left.body: Record values on a unit (odometer, temperature, status, …) via QR portal or API. Manage fields under Work → Unit measurements; enable per category and unit and link fields. History in admin; webhook unit.measurement.recorded.

left.title: Photos
left.body: Up to 4 photos per issue or completion (resized on the device before upload). Also: up to 4 unit photos and a background photo per unit for the QR portal. Visible immediately in the back office; reporter photos on the public portal only after approval.

left.title: GPS
left.body: Per category: “Allow GPS location” for mobile units (vehicle, machine, …). Capture location via the portal; history in the back office, open in Maps.

right.title: Calendar
right.body: Month, week and day views of tasks, issues and reservations. From the calendar you can also print the briefing for that day.

right.title: Briefing
right.body: Printable report of open tasks for the selected day, grouped by team. Available from Dashboard, Tasks and Calendar — useful at shift start.

right.title: Reports
right.body: On search screens (issues, tasks, Time, reservations, unit checks, unit measurements, ESG): Download report — CSV (table for Excel) or print (Ctrl+P to PDF). Print follows the backoffice list card layout where possible; Time shows a timesheet. Same filters as the list (max. 5000 rows). Later: Organisation → Reports for saved templates.

right.title: Time
right.body: Time is WinProx’s punch clock: clock in/out, breaks, presence and timesheets. Each clock-in, clock-out or move on Clock Point needs a fresh QR scan on site (an open tab does not count); breaks can continue without a new scan. Clock Point remains the sign-in QR (name + icon, task list) even without Time. Time is included in the trial and in every WinProx plan. CIAO (NSSO) is on request, with no extra fee; a superuser enables it. Name lookup on a clock point is scoped to that site; workers only appear on assigned sites (except floater teams). One open shift per worker: at another Clock Point you see where you are clocked in and can move presence (same shift, with a hop note). Presence optionally shows the worker portrait in the round avatar (otherwise the initial). Optional CIAO (RSZ Check In and Out): real-time IN/OUT + breaks for cleaning; request via info@winprox.app (superuser enables it); NISS on worker; DDT on location. Construction/concrete scope (CIAO) follows behind a feature flag until RSZ go-live (~Apr 2027). Clock Point sign-in is bound to one phone per worker; another device is refused until an admin or team leader allows a new device. Optional: 4-digit PIN on Clock Point and GPS at the punch (indoor punches still proceed without a signal). A too-quick move between Clock Points (within 5 min) appears as an alarm. The personal icon is hidden after sign-in. API clock-in (POST /api/v1/time/clock-in) does not bind a phone — that applies only to Clock Point QR. A bound device can be released via admin, team leader or API (time:write). On the Clock Point portal (after sign-in) there is a My hours tile (only your own shifts for the selected month) and optionally (Settings, off by default) an Evacuation list tile: only a signed-in field worker sees who is clocked in (including colleagues with a punch-clock profile), after confirming that the consultation is exceptional and is logged (first name, last name, date and time). Admins reset device, PIN and icon via People → Teams → Edit. An administrator or staff user can clock a worker in manually at a Clock Point (e.g. forgotten phone): no device bind, required reason in the audit log, Clocked in manually pill on presence and hours. API: POST /api/v1/time/manual-clock-in (admin source, does not bind a phone). Per team you can set a minimum break (e.g. 30 minutes): on clock-out it is counted on the timesheet if less or no live break was clocked, without an extra Clock Point break or CIAO event. On Time → Hours an admin can still apply or correct the minimum. API: POST /api/v1/time/work-shifts/{id}/apply-required-break. Managers plan shifts in Time → Roster (Excel-like: codes or free times per day). Publishing does not send anything to RSZ; the punch clock remains actual time. Week view can show or hide weekends; saving with weekends off leaves Sat/Sun unchanged. Optionally a group in the same cell (D1/G1 or 07:00-12:00/G1); roster code per unit, unique per location. Week or month view. Absences (leave, time off in lieu, sick) via Shift types: full day, no hours. Publishing shows My roster on Clock Point (badge) and is not sent to the NSSO. Admin: planned vs clocked (deviation immediately, including today; missing punch after the planned end). Location filter hides floaters; optional home group and section rows. Optional GPS work visits (Settings): clock-in opens paid time without location proof; start/stop work on the location pin (customer) or a unit with a fixed GPS pin requires fresh GPS within the radius (default 250 m). Set the location pin under Locations (red Maps icon; paste as lat, lng). Same field for a unit pin under Advanced portal options. Clock-out is allowed anywhere; an open visit is closed first. CIAO then follows visit IN/OUT instead of clock in/out. Back office: Work → Work visits shows the history; Time → Presence shows an open visit and Time → Hours shows visits per shift. The public homepage does not suggest nearby companies. API: POST /api/v1/time/work-visits/start and .../end; webhooks time.visit.started / time.visit.ended. After clock-in Clock Point shows where you need to go today (locations only, work planned for today), with a GPS icon to Google Maps; Start work on site. Inspection stops are under Open tasks (description, priority, status, next stop, Unit check button). With an open work visit you can start and complete team tasks (optional note and photos) and do the next inspection stop (unit check).

right.title: Reservations
right.body: For shared resources with a time slot (room, vehicle, key). Category Reservable + Allow reservations per unit (off by default). Guest books via unit QR (hold + email confirmation). Manage via Reservations menu and calendar.

right.title: ESG & Compliance
right.body: ESG = Environmental, Social & Governance: readings for environment, safety and compliance (energy, inspections, …). Optional module on WinProx Corporate: indicators, measurements and follow-up tasks for recurring checks. Record via portal, back office or API.

right.title: IoT Connect
right.body: Sensor gateways send events; alarms become an approved issue + task. Measurements → ESG. WinProx Corporate only. Gateway token (also without the full REST API).

right.title: API & webhooks
right.body: REST API tokens and outbound webhooks (HMAC) under Settings. Connect issues, tasks, unit checks, unit measurements, ESG, … IoT ingest via a separate gateway token. See also the API & Webhooks sheet and the technical fact sheet.

right.title: Multi-tenant
right.body: Each organisation has its own environment with limits per subscription (WinProx 10/25/50 seats + Corporate): seats (active colleagues + active workers without a linked user_id; colleague + punch-clock profile = one seat). Units and documents follow the seat count (10/25/50). Locations and photos are unlimited.

right.title: Branding & QR
right.body: Organisation logo, portal background and portal colours (background and button colour) under Settings; unit photos and a background photo per unit. Avery or A6/A5/A4 sticker formats — print-ready.

right.title: Work menu
right.body: Via Organisation → Settings → Work menu settings (administrator): toggle Calendar, Reservations, Inspection rounds and Unit measurements per organisation in the sidebar. Off = no backoffice access; QR on units that already had the feature keeps working (grandfather). A starter template sets a limited work menu. You can turn on Reservations, unit measurements and other extras later. Removing the starter template does not change the work menu.

right.title: AI translation
right.body: After approval, texts are queued for translation (issues, tasks, documents, announcements, …). WinProx fills the other languages periodically via local AI (no external AI cloud), typically daily — with no guaranteed turnaround. Organisation admins can correct translations manually; there is no per-organisation on/off switch.

right.title: No app required
right.body: Everything runs in the browser. Back office is desktop-first; field and QR portals are mobile-first. No App Store, no install.

full.title: Roles
full.body: Admin — full control + subscription · Employee — day-to-day follow-up (no billing/accounts) · Worker — field work via Clock Point + unit QR, without WinProx login · Team leader — release icons and coordinate via the Clock Point portal.

full.title: Back-office login
full.body: Admins and employees sign in with email + password, or via **Sign in with Microsoft** (Microsoft Entra). Only existing WinProx accounts; the Microsoft email must match. Workers stay on Clock Point QR (name + icon), without Microsoft sign-in. Connecting other software uses API tokens, not this login.

technical.label: Technical fact sheet
technical.tagline: Facility issues: QR → tasks → completion · SaaS for operational teams
technical.intro: Overview for IT / security. WinProx is a multi-tenant web application (Laravel + MySQL) where each customer organisation has its own isolated environment. Optional Time roster: planned shifts per worker (draft or published), week or month, half-open overlap. Absences (leave, time off in lieu, sick) fill a full day. API `/api/v1/time/schedule` (time:read / time:write) and webhooks `time.schedule.*`. Published roster: Clock Point tile My roster (own shifts only) with a badge. Admin: planned vs clocked. Optional group slot (roster code on the unit) and home group on the worker; location filter hides floaters.
technical.footer_left: WinProx · info@winprox.app · Product overview, not legal advice or an SLA.
technical.footer_right: Questions? We are happy to walk through the DPA, subprocessors and integrations.

left.title: Hosting
items: Production on **Linux** (EU), at **Cloud86**.
Access via **HTTPS** (encrypted connection, TLS).
Stack: PHP 8.2+, Laravel 12, Livewire, MySQL, Vite frontend.
Email via SMTP in the EU; billing by yearly invoice (no online checkout).
Pricing: from **€7 / seat / month** (10 seats + 10 units), **€6** (25), **€5** (50). Billed yearly by invoice. Corporate is custom.

left.title: Backups
items: Automatic **daily** backups via Cloud86 (files + database), retained for **7 days**.
**RPO ≈ 24 hours**: in the worst case you lose data since the last nightly backup (Recovery Point Objective = max. acceptable data loss).
**RTO: best effort, typically within 1 business day** (Recovery Time Objective = time until the service is available again after restore).
On full organisation deletion: separate technical SQL snapshot **without media**, max. **30 days** (not the same as a disaster-recovery backup).

left.title: Database
items: **MySQL**, relational model per tenant.
Strict **tenant isolation**: every query/API call stays within the organisation.
No shared visibility between customers.
**Location scope:** pivot tables location_user and location_worker; teams.clocks_all_locations for floaters; workers.user_id links colleague to worker profile.

left.title: Permissions
items: **Admin**: everything (users, company, subscription, teams).
**Employee**: operational (issues, tasks, locations) — no account/billing management.
**Worker / team leader**: complete tasks via the field portal; team leaders can release icons and a bound phone.
Every action is checked: you only get what your role allows (**least privilege**). API keys get separate permissions — e.g. “read issues” without access to everything.

Operational reports: filtered CSV or print on issues, tasks, Time, reservations, unit checks, unit measurements and ESG — for users who may view those lists. Print follows the list layout where possible; Time = timesheet. Separate from the GDPR account export (Settings → Privacy & data export).

Work menu: tenant columns work_menu_*_enabled; sidebar and backoffice routes via TenantWorkMenuAccess; starter template sets defaults via UpdateTenantWorkMenuAction (removing template does not revert menu).

left.title: API
items: **REST API v1** (fixed URLs + HTTP methods) with **JSON** responses (standard data format). Documentation in-app + docs.
Incl. issues, tasks, locations, units (incl. external ID), teams, workers, unit check (also inbound via external unit ID), unit measurements, ESG, translations.
Available on **Corporate** (trial on request).
IoT ingest separately via gateway token (Corporate).

right.title: GDPR
items: **Customer = controller**; WinProx = **processor**.
Framework: EU GDPR + Belgian Act of 30 July 2018.
Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and subprocessor list available.
Data export (account), self-service organisation deletion, retention periods documented.

Data stays in the **EU** (hosting/email). Stripe EU/US when paying. With **Sign in with Microsoft**, the user is sent to Microsoft Entra ID (Microsoft, EU/US); WinProx receives email (and possibly name) to match the existing account.

Optional email confirmation for QR reports: temporary draft storage until the link; unverified drafts are deleted automatically (typically 60 minutes, including photos). The confirmation mail is only sent to a valid address that is not marked undeliverable (bounce). Unsubscribing from marketing mail does not block this confirmation. No user account.

Optional **CIAO** forwarding (RSZ Check In and Out): when enabled, WinProx stores NISS (encrypted) and sends presence registrations to the **Belgian NSSO/RSZ** (public authority / customer legal duty). RSZ is not a WinProx marketing sub-processor; transfer is for compliance. Customer OAuth credentials stay encrypted at rest. An applied team break on the timesheet is not an extra RSZ IN/OUT. With GPS work visits: clock in/out are not sent to the NSSO; visit start = IN, visit end = OUT. Breaks during a visit remain OUT/IN.

Optional planned roster: shifts and absences (leave, time off in lieu, sick) entered by the customer; Clock Point shows only the worker’s own published roster. Sick codes are the customer’s choice; WinProx stores them as processor.

right.title: Availability
items: Available 24/7 as SaaS (browser + QR portals).
Unit QR: a loaded page stays usable without network for tasks, reports and unit checks; it syncs when connectivity returns. Clock Point punches stay online and need a fresh QR scan.
Planned maintenance preferably outside business hours, with notice where possible.
Formal uptime SLA: available contractually on request.

right.title: Authentication
items: Back office: email + password (stored hashed), sessions.

Self-service sign-up requires **email verification**: the account only works after clicking the link in the confirmation mail. The confirmation mail is only sent to a valid address that is not marked undeliverable (bounce). Unsubscribing from marketing mail does not block this confirmation. Unverified sign-ups are automatically and completely deleted after 7 days.

**SSO** (one work login via Microsoft Entra): for admins and employees on desktop (**Sign in with Microsoft**). Only existing WinProx accounts (email must match the Microsoft account); email + password still works. No automatic new accounts. Workers stay on Clock Point QR (name + icon). Connecting other software (Ultimo, IWMS, …) uses API tokens, not SSO.
API: personal **access key** (Bearer token via Laravel Sanctum). Revocable; with scopes = which actions the key may perform.
Workers: **no email login** — Clock Point QR + name + personal icon (or optional PIN). One phone per worker; the icon is hidden after sign-in.
Offline field actions on the unit QR go through POST /portal/field-sync with the device cookie (no API token). The same client_id does not create a duplicate issue or task change.
Reporters: public QR portal without an account. Optional mailbox proof (category and unit): no login; the issue is created only after the link in the mail.
Colleague with **punch-clock team** gets a linked worker profile for Clock Point (name + icon); does not count twice towards the licence.

right.title: Security
items: HTTPS; hashed passwords; revocable API tokens.
**CSRF protection**: prevents another website from secretly performing actions as a logged-in user.
Tenant scoping; audit/activity logs.
Webhooks with **HMAC-SHA256** signature (proof the message comes from WinProx).
API: max. **60 requests/minute** per token.
Support access: exceptional, read-only by default.

Time Clock Point: a fresh QR scan per clock-in, clock-out or move (an open tab/poll is not enough). One phone per worker (refuse + audit on another device). There is no switch-worker control (including on the icon/PIN step) and after sign-in the Sign in heading is hidden; Sign out returns to icon/PIN without clocking out, and the phone stays bound until an admin or team leader releases it. Optional hashed PIN and GPS (punch proceeds without a signal). API clock-in does not bind a phone. Manual clock-in in back office (admin/staff) does not bind a phone. My hours (tile after sign-in): only the signed-in worker’s own shifts. My roster: only that worker’s published roster for the month. Evacuation list (optional in Settings, off by default; tile after sign-in): names only after confirming the consultation is exceptional; each view is logged (first name, last name, date and time). Views from today light up Time attention on the dashboard and on Presence. Time → Alarms keeps the full list (date and time, newest first). Admins release phone, PIN and icon via People → Teams → Edit. During an open work visit Clock Point shows the current location and next stop at the top. Today locations follow inspection-round stop order. Clock Point stores an essential device cookie (about 1 year). An applied team break on the timesheet is not an RSZ/CIAO event (no fake IN/OUT). GPS work visits: fresh GPS at click time (maximumAge 0) to start/stop work on a location pin or unit pin; clock-in stays without a GPS gate. After clock-in (GPS work visits on): Today card with planned destinations and Navigate (Google Maps); Start work only on site. With an open visit: start/complete team tasks on Clock Point; next inspection stop (unit check) on site.

right.title: Webhooks
items: Outbound HTTP POST on events (incl. issue/task status, unit check, unit measurement, ESG, GPS, Time/CIAO). time.visit.started / time.visit.ended.
Configured under Settings → API; secret for verification.
Automatic retries on failure (several attempts with increasing delay).
Same plan requirement as API (Corporate).
With optional email confirmation, the **issue created** event fires only after the link, not when the form is submitted on the portal.

full.title: Spam & abuse (limits)
items: **Public QR issues** (per device/IP, per unit): max. **1 issue per 3 minutes**; max. **5 issues per 30 minutes** on the same unit; max. **20 issues per hour** across all units of the same organisation. (Signed-in workers are exempt.)
**Worker sign-in (icon)**: after **2 wrong icon choices** the worker is locked until a team leader or admin releases them.
**Back-office login** (email/password): passwords hashed; no separate app rate limit on failed logins (can be strengthened via infra/contract).

Extra: QR issues on the public portal stay **invisible until approval**. Optional email confirmation (category and unit) holds the report until the email link; existing QR limits count at submit. API has its own rate limit (60/min).

full.title: AI (Artificial Intelligence)
items: After approval, operational texts (issues, tasks, units, announcements, …) are queued for AI translation.
Assistant knowledge base answers (superuser) use the same Ollama pipeline as operational content.
Runs on a **local Ollama instance** — no ChatGPT / external AI cloud for this feature.
WinProx runs translations **periodically** (typically daily), **with no guaranteed turnaround**. Organisation admins can **correct translations manually**. No per-organisation on/off switch.
No generative “AI assistant” that autonomously decides customer processes — translation is support, not decision-making.

api_webhooks.label: API & Webhooks
api_webhooks.tagline: Integrate WinProx with your existing software via APIs and webhooks.
api_webhooks.highlight: WinProx is not a replacement for existing IWMS or ERP systems. Thanks to APIs and webhooks, WinProx works alongside them.
api_webhooks.intro: WinProx is built so other software can use the same data, issues, tasks and unit checks as WinProx itself. Manage and read docs under Settings → API. Desktop **Sign in with Microsoft** is not an API integration: other software uses tokens, not SSO. Time roster: GET/PUT `/api/v1/time/schedule`, POST `.../copy` and `.../publish` (time:read / time:write). Events: `time.schedule.saved`, `time.schedule.copied`, `time.schedule.published`, `time.shift_type.saved`. Absences (leave, time off in lieu, sick) are shift types without hours. Published roster: Clock Point My roster with a badge. Admin: planned vs clocked. Optional group slot (roster code) and home group; location filter hides floaters.
api_webhooks.footer_right: See also: Features overview · Technical fact sheet

left.title: Why APIs and webhooks?
left.body: With the API and webhooks, WinProx can work with existing software. For example:
items: automatically forward an issue to your IWMS, CMMS or ERP;
forward a unit check (OK/Not OK) to your external facility software;
record a unit measurement (POST /units/{unit}/measurements);
receive a unit check from your external facility software (via external unit ID);
synchronise tasks with an ERP system;
show data in Power BI;
let IoT sensors create issues automatically;
connect to your own software or Microsoft Power Automate.
left.emphasis: Your central system (IWMS, ERP, BI) stays in the lead — WinProx complements it on the shop floor.

rows: Your system asks WinProx for something
WinProx sends a message to your system

left.title: What this is not
items: Not every action is available via the API. Some parts are intentionally read-only or support only specific actions. That keeps integrations safe and manageable.
You manage webhooks in the app, not via the API.
A generic inbound webhook endpoint for arbitrary external systems is not a product feature yet (IoT and Stripe have their own paths).
API & outbound webhooks: Corporate (trial API on request).

right.title: REST API
right.body: The API lets other software safely retrieve data or perform actions inside WinProx. Communication uses standard REST endpoints and JSON.
items: **Access:** personal access token (Bearer). Revocable. Per token you choose permissions (scopes), e.g. read issues only.
**Organisation boundary:** each token belongs to one organisation; you never see another customer’s data.
**Safety:** request rate limit per minute. Optional Idempotency-Key so a repeated request does not create a duplicate action.
**IoT separately:** sensors use a gateway token (Corporate), not the same API token.

rows: Issues, Tasks, Locations, Units, Teams, Workers, Unit checks, Unit measurements

Clock in/out, shifts (API clock-in does not bind a phone); release bound device; manual clock-in (POST /api/v1/time/manual-clock-in, admin source, does not bind a phone); apply minimum break (POST /api/v1/time/work-shifts/{id}/apply-required-break); teams expose required_break_minutes; GPS work visits POST /api/v1/time/work-visits/start (unit_id or location_id) and .../end (time:write); webhooks time.visit.started / time.visit.ended

right.title: Outbound webhooks
right.body: WinProx sends an HTTP POST to a URL you provide whenever something happens.
items: **Setup:** Settings → API → Webhooks (URL + which events). The secret is shown once — store it safely.
**Proof of origin:** each message has an HMAC signature (verifiable with your secret).
**Reliability:** if delivery fails, WinProx retries (with increasing delay). Deliveries appear in a log.

**Other events include:** issue created / approved / status changed · task created / started / completed · Time (incl. CIAO presence) · GPS · ESG · reservations · test button · unit check recorded. With email confirmation: **issue created** only after the link. time.visit.started / time.visit.ended.
right.emphasis: Example: a worker completes a task. WinProx automatically sends a webhook to your external system (IWMS, CMMS or ERP) so a work order can be updated immediately.

full.title: Ready for integration
full.body: WinProx is designed to work alongside existing systems. Suitable for integration with, among others:
items: IWMS / facility management
CMMS / maintenance systems
ERP
Microsoft Power Automate
Power BI
Custom software
IoT platforms
full.emphasis: Have an existing IT landscape? We are happy to explore how WinProx fits. Contact: info@winprox.app · Documentation: Settings → API → Docs
